half: Roja L. Rivera is a thesis adviser with one thesis recorded in this repository, which was advised in 2026. Their research focus within this repository involves online and distance learning and student assessment and achievement. They supervised one thesis titled "Factors of Self-Regulated Learning in the Online Component of Blended Learning Among Private Junior High School Students" in 2026. This specific work, completed by Mark Benlor Buenaventura Sy, utilizes an explanatory-sequential mixed-method design to investigate how private junior high school students in the Philippines manage their learning processes during the online components of blended learning. The research topics covered in this supervision include blended learning, e-learning, the Philippine education system, and self-regulated learning. Because the repository only contains one supervised thesis and no personal publications, further information regarding their specific academic strengths or long-term research trajectory is not available from the provided data.

Roja L. Rivera is a thesis adviser with a research focus that includes online and distance learning as well as student assessment and achievement. Based on the items available in this repository, their work is centered on the intersection of these two areas. Specifically, their research interests involve the mechanisms of learning within digital environments and how these environments impact student outcomes. In the single thesis they have advised in this repository, which was completed in 2026, the research investigated the factors of self-regulated learning within the online component of blended learning among private junior high school students. This specific study utilized an explanatory-sequential mixed-method design to examine how students in the Philippine education system manage their learning processes during online instructional periods. Because there is only one thesis listed, it is difficult to establish a broad pattern of supervision or to determine if these topics represent their primary long-term research trajectory. However, the available evidence shows a clear interest in the practical application of blended learning and e-learning frameworks. The research they have overseen touches upon the complexities of how students navigate self-regulated learning when transitioning between physical and digital classrooms. This focus suggests an interest in the pedagogical shifts occurring within modern educational systems, particularly regarding how assessment and achievement are influenced by the structure of online components. At this time, Roja L. Rivera has no authored articles present in this repository, so their individual scholarly publications cannot be reviewed here. Their presence in the repository is defined by their role in supervising student research rather than by their own published datasets or theoretical papers. The single instance of supervision recorded occurred in 2026, which is also the latest year represented in this repository. Consequently, the evidence regarding their specific strengths in certain methodologies or their capacity for supervising large numbers of students is limited. They have supervised one student, Mark Benlor Buenaventura Sy, on a topic that integrates mixed-method designs with educational psychology concepts like self-regulation. While the scope of their work in this repository is currently narrow, the subject matter indicates a specialization in the digital transition of traditional schooling and the resulting impact on student autonomy and achievement metrics. Future entries in the repository would be required to determine if they continue to focus on the Philippine education system or if they expand their supervision to other academic levels or different methodological approaches. As it stands, their profile is characterized by a specific investigation into the online components of blended learning environments.
